Method of Attack: Stealing plaintext passwords from website source code via a Chrome extension
Capturing HTML source code on login attempts using regex
Abusing CSS selectors to extract user inputs via '.value' function
Performing element substitution to replace JS-obfuscated fields with unsafe password fields
Impacted Systems: Google Chrome extensions (approx. 17,300 extensions with permissions to extract sensitive info)
Websites storing passwords in plaintext in HTML source code (e.g., gmail.com, cloudflare.com)
Websites vulnerable to DOM API input extraction (e.g., facebook.com, citibank.com)
Websites exposing SSNs in plaintext in source code (irs.gov, capitalone.com, usenix.org)
Websites exposing credit card details in plaintext (amazon.com)
Attack Vector: Unrestricted access to DOM tree by browser extensions
Content scripts accessing user input fields and source code
Indicators of Compromise: Extensions with permissions to access sensitive website data (approx. 17,300 in Chrome Web Store)
190 extensions accessing password fields and storing values in variables
Websites with plaintext passwords or sensitive data in HTML source code
Extension passing Google Chrome Web Store review despite malicious capabilities
